title: So the man moved acts by a necessity of infallibility yet keeps a real power not to act
source_text: XVIII. Igitur, juxta hanc doctrinam, homo ad hoc vel illud agendum efficaciter a Deo motus, vel judicii proprii dictamine impulsus, necessario quidem agit necessitate quadam infallibilitatis; sed simul tamen veram non agendi potestatem retinet. Et potest quidem non agere, sed certo tamen acturus est: neque contingere potest ut carentia actionis conjungatur unquam cum tali judicio, vel cum ejusmodi Dei motione.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore, according to this doctrine, man efficaciously moved by God to doing this or that, or impelled by the dictate of his own judgment, acts indeed necessarily by a certain necessity of infallibility; but at the same time yet retains a true power of not acting. And he can indeed not act, but yet will certainly act: nor can it happen that the lack of the action should ever be joined with such a judgment, or with a motion of God of that kind.
pass_b_english: On this teaching, then, a man whom God effectively moves to do this or that, or whom the dictate of his own judgment drives to it, does act necessarily, with a necessity of infallibility, while still keeping a real power not to act.
He is able not to act, yet he will surely act; and the absence of the act can never be found together with such a judgment or with such a motion from God.

lemmas.gloss: by a certain necessity of infallibility

choices.why: Kept as the technical phrase both Reformed parties use; it marks the necessity that removes the power to act otherwise, as against a necessity of infallibility.
